## `client.groups`

The `groups` resource of the platform API.

### `client.groups.create`

Signature: `client.groups.create(name: str, *, override_reason: str | None = None) -> Group`

Create a group.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | `str` | required | The group's unique name. |
| `override_reason` | `str | None` | `None` | Why, 10 to 500 characters on one line, to create the group although an access file manages its scope (an audited override, for an administrator of the instance). |

### `client.groups.list`

Signature: `client.groups.list(*, search: str | None = None, limit: int | None = None, cursor: str | None = None) -> list[Group]`

List groups, newest first.

The groups of one page; `list_page` also returns the cursor of the next one, and `iter` walks every page.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `search` | `str | None` | `None` | Only groups whose name contains this text, in any letter case. |
| `limit` | `int | None` | `None` | Most groups returned (1 to 200); `None` leaves it to the server (100). |
| `cursor` | `str | None` | `None` | A previous page's `next_cursor`. Send the same `search` with every page. |

Returns: `list of Group`. Newest first.

|---|---|---|---|
